articles.headline: A Sketch of the Life and Character of the Late Rev. Richard Roberson (part 1)
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: About the year of our Lord, 1796, was born of a woman, a son, who afterwards received the name of Richard Roberson. His birth, according to all the facts we can get in relation to him, took place in the State of Maryland... he was put out under a man by the name of Zebulon [VERIFY] Fergerson, in north east Maryland... emigrated to Bucks county... about the year 1819... married, before he made any profession of religion, at Sandy Run, Bucks county, Pa.; class leader and steward on the Bucks county circuit; exhorter; licensed to preach by the Rev. Jacob Richardson, itinerant on the Bucks county circuit. (To be continued.) N.B. Weaver asks for copies of the Philadelphia and New York Conference minutes 1832-1848 for writing a sketch of Father Roberson's life.

articles.headline: Meetings and Demonstrations (Emancipation Proclamation, Jan. 1, 1863)
articles.summary: In honor to the President's proclamation there were services, we believe, held in every colored church in the city of Philadelphia. In Bethel Church there were meetings morning and night. There was also a combination of the Presbyterian Churches. They were all at Mr. Gibb's Church in Seventh St., in the morning; in the afternoon they combined together at the St. Mary St. Church, and at eight they all met in Rev. Mr. Reeve's Church, Lombard St. The St. Thomas Church held a meeting in the fore part of the day, and so did the Baptist Churches, we believe. Wesley Church, Lombard St., of which Rev. John A. Williams is pastor, had a strong demonstration morning, noon, and night... (Also named, reading uncertain: Walter Jackson [VERIFY] (speaker (Rev.) at Wesley Church, Jan. 1, 1863).)

articles.headline: Lecture (Weaver's address to the mothers of Burlington)
articles.summary: On last Tuesday night, the 6th inst., we were invited to deliver an address to the mothers of Burlington, and others. They far excelled our people here in the city of Philadelphia...

articles.headline: On the Life of Rev. Richard Roberson, No. 2
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: (Continued from last Number.) Verbal history informs us that Brother Roberson was admitted into the Church by Bp. Freeman ordained Elder the same day for Sierra Leone, Africa; Roberson for Hayti. In the fall of 1823 Brother Roberson and his dear wife Tamar [VERIFY] sailed for Hayti. (To be continued.)

articles.headline: Life of Rev. Richard Roberson, No. 4
articles.author: Elisha Weaver
articles.summary: (Continued from last number.) In our last, we left off with Father Roberson's return from Hayti, to meet with his conference for the ordination of an elder... The Conference was presided over by Rev. Richard Allen, the first Bishop of the African Methodist Episcopal Church... the Rev. Richard Roberson was the first to convey [the gospel] to the Haytiens... The motion to ordain was carried, and he, Roberson, was ordained an elder... he sets sail... with a hope of seeing his wife Tamar, whom he had left behind in Hayti... Port au Prince... articles.headline: Can't Be Quiet (proposed Pennsylvania exclusion amendment)
articles.summary: We were told sometime ago by a man opposed to the policy of the administration, that the Government had been legislating for the negroes for the last twenty years; and as soon as this war was over, the negroes and abolitionists would have to leave... If we are to take the following bill, reported and referred in the Pennsylvania Legislature, the colored man has a foretaste of what is to come... prints 'Negroes and Mulattoes', Sections 1-3: no negro or mulatto to come into or settle in the State; fines $100-$500 for employing them; fines to fund colonization.

articles.summary: We left home for Washington, D. C., on Friday night, the 16th ult., ten minutes after 12 M., and arrived in Washington a few minutes after 6 o'clock, A. M., and stopped with brother James H. Wright and lady, one of the first families in Washington.
people: pastor (Rev.), Baltimore; thanked for the collection after the editor's lecture there

articles.headline: The Life of Rev. Richard Roberson, No. V
articles.summary: We left off with Brother Roberson's return to Hayti, after his ordination in the United States. He now enters upon his new mission with vigor, on behalf of the A. M. E. Church. He looks forward to his success under God, in building up Zion, in establishing a branch of the African M. E. Church in that city, the capitol of the Isle of Hayti.
people: subject (Rev.); A.M.E. missionary in Hayti from about 1824-25, gravely ill there with scarlet fever

articles.headline: A Meritorious Act
articles.summary: Passing Front and Chestnut on Saturday last, we observed a large number of soldiers with blankets, haversacks, and muskets on their backs as though they were en route to the scene of their country's conflict. There was a woman on the corner selling apples. She took up her basket and crossed to where the soldiers were and as they passed handed each man an apple.

articles.headline: Proclamation of Emancipation (letter from Camden, N. J., January 17th, 1863)
articles.author: O. H. D.
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: We received with joy on the first day of January the most important and far-reaching document that has emanated from the pen of President Lincoln since his inauguration. Nothing less a document, than one declaring all persons held as slaves in the States therein, designated, henceforth free.

articles.headline: Eulogy on the Life of Samuel Ringgold
articles.summary: This eulogy was delivered at Bensalem, by the Elder of the Frankford Circuit, on the 27th of January, 1863. Samuel Ringgold, the subject of this eulogy, was born in 1843 in Philadelphia. His parents died when he was quite young, and he was thus left to wander from place to place at an early age, until he lost his health for want of the care and comforts of this life. At length he providentially fell into the hands of George and Rachel Longster, who took him as their own child and tenderly cared for him.
people: deceased; born 1843 in Philadelphia, died at Bensalem, Bucks Co., aged 19; embraced religion while with the Longsters

articles.headline: The State of the Country and Colored People; The Call for Colored Soldiers; Colored Soldiers
articles.summary: For more than a century this country has bowed to the cruel villany of oppression, perpetrated upon a portion of God's own likeness or creation, in the most inhuman and unchristian manner that ever was witnessed in a land of civilization and liberty.

articles.headline: Brother Weaver: Macedonian Church, Camden, supper for the pastor
articles.author: Peter Gardiner [VERIFY]
articles.summary: Brother Weaver: Please publish this acknowledgment; we must not despise the day of small things. Notwithstanding, the Macedonian Church, Camden, is small, and its members are poor, yet they have done something commendable. On the 7th inst., a few of the sisters, viz., Mary Ann Mackey, Emeline Vanslyke, Emeline Anderson, Lydia Hamilton, Elizabeth Parker, Sophia Brown, and Jane Johnson, understanding that I had received but a little of my salary this year, formed themselves into a committee, and made a delicious supper.

articles.headline: Washington correspondence (letter signed H. M. T.)
articles.author: H. M. T.
articles.summary: Congress is holding very late night sessions. I called in the House of Representatives on Wednesday evening, while they were discussing the merits and demerits of a pending bill, for the indemnification of the President of the United States ... Dated Washington, Feb. 21st, 1863. Washington news only: the conscript bill and the colored soldier bill; Benjamin T. Tanner on the withdrawal of the L. S. C. Society and 15th Street Presbyterian delegates from 'the convention' (Rev. Henry Wilson, William Slade named); Recorder sales in Washington (Bro. Moore, James L. Thomas, Rev. H. J. Rhodes agents); Rev. J. M. Brown's Repository article at the Indiana Conference and the Repository's poor sale in Indianapolis (Rev. William Davis, Dr. Revels named); Prof. Fowler's lectures; a contraband boy stabbed by a white boy named Flanagan.

articles.headline: The Negro Soldier
articles.author: William Steward
articles.summary: Thomas H. Benton in his 'Thirty Years' View,' said that his opposition to slavery dated as far back as 1804, when a student in Tennessee ... Abraham Lincoln and his practical associates, when they found it necessary ... saw fit to heap a burden upon 'the race to which I belong,' and call upon them to show their patriotism to a country which has always denied them the right to be men. Signed William Steward, Bridgeton, N. J., Feb. 17th, 1863.

articles.headline: Letter on the church at New Brunswick, N.J.
articles.author: Theodore Gould
articles.summary: Mr. Editor: Perhaps it would be of interest to your readers to hear how our Church in New Brunswick is prospering. It was thought that we should lose our church in that place ... So God, through the labors of his servant, Brother Offer (the stated pastor), is showing that he has a people in that place ... In company with the Elder, Mr. Moore, of Trenton, N. J., I visited the congregation ... a festival realizing fifteen dollars ... Brother Offer has organized a school numbering between eighty and one hundred children. Signed Rev. Theodore Gould [VERIFY], P[rince]ton [?], N. J.

Those of our agents who have not yet done so, will please remit by return mail ... those of our city friends who have not yet found opportunity to pay up their subscriptions for the year, would please call at our office (619 Pine St.) and settle up ...

One piece called, 'I would not live always,' is dedicated to Bethel Sabbath school, and the other is dedicated to the members of Bethel Choir of Philadelphia. The price of the latter is 15 cents, and the former 6 cents. They can be had at the A. M. E. Book Store, No. 619 Pine street.

articles.headline: Mob Law in Detroit (editorial)
articles.summary: We have to chronicle one of the most disgraceful, inhuman, and heathen-like scenes that ever stained the pages of history, in the city of Detroit ... What have the colored people done that they should be thus treated? Even here, in the city of Philadelphia, in many places it is almost impossible for a respectable colored person to walk the streets without being insulted by a set of blackguards and cowards ...

articles.summary: Rev. Peter Gardiner, Elder of the Camden, New Jersey, circuit, has been very much indisposed for a week or more ... The Rev. William Alston, of the St. Thomas' Church, preached in Bethel Church last Sabbath afternoon ... The Rev. Mr. Gibbs, of the 1st Presbyterian Church, (colored) has been indisposed for the last two or three weeks ... Also Rev. Mr. Reeves, of the Lombard Street Presbyterian Church, was so unwell as to be unable to officiate on last Sabbath. There is considerable sickness in the city. Our very active, energetic, efficient, and skilful Dr. Wilson, is kept constantly on the run ... Sister Campbell, the wife of Rev. J. P. Campbell, has, for several weeks, been quite ill ... Rev. A. L. Stanford's wife has been very low ...
people: elder of the Camden, N. J. circuit (Rev.); ill
St. Thomas' Church (Rev.); preached at Bethel

articles.headline: Colored Soldiers (Philadelphia stir)
articles.summary: There is a considerable stir in our city in relation to colored soldiers. Some of these are going to join the Massachusetts company; and others are preparing to join in the anticipated company from this state. They are awaiting Governor Curtin's motion. It is thought that he is very favorable to it ...

articles.headline: Acknowledgments
articles.summary: Paulsboro [?], N. J.: Edward P. Johnson, James H. Trott [?]. Woodbury, N. J.: Miss Sarah M. Andrews, Miss M. M. Stevens, Miss Hannah Lisson [?], Miss Margarette Harmon [?]. St. Louis: E. Pines and others (per Rev. M. M. Clark). Baltimore: Rev. James Lynch. Lawrence, Kansas: Lewis N. Johnson. New Garden, Ind.: James Buckner, Asbury Benson. Moorestown, N. J.: Franklin Taylor per Mr. Theo. Coonle [?]; George Thomas. Georgetown, D. C.: Rev. H. J. Rhodes. Washington: Mr. James L. Thomas. (NJ names not linked: several surnames blurred.)

articles.headline: Notice (John Andrews disclaims debts of his wife Elizabeth Andrews)
articles.author: John Andrews
articles.summary: Woodbury, March 23d, 1863. This is to certify that on Tuesday, the 17th inst., my wife, Elizabeth Andrews, left my bed and board, without any provocation whatever. I therefore warn and forbid all persons harboring her on my account, for I will not pay or be responsible for no debts that she may contract from this date. John Andrews. (Woodbury, N. J.; text only.)

events.name: Germantown A.M.E. Church dedicated
events.description: The Germantown A. M. E. Church was dedicated on the afternoon of Christmas day 1862. The Rev. W. D. W. Schureman (printed 'Schuramen'/'Schureman'), the Elder, had extended an invitation to all. The church is small but arranged 'with much taste and neatness.'

events.name: Freedmen Association of Union A.M.E. Church receives donation from Young Men's Reading Assembly No. 1
events.description: Notice dated December the 25th [VERIFY], 1862: Henry Davis, Chairman of the Committee of the Freedmen Association of the A. M. E. Union Church in Philadelphia, received of Mr. Isaac Williams, accompanied by Mr. George Mercer, ten dollars from the Young Men's Reading Assembly, No. 1, of Northern Liberties, Philadelphia.
attendees: chairman, committee of the Freedmen Association, Union A.M.E. Church
Young Men's Reading Assembly No. 1, Northern Liberties
Young Men's Reading Assembly No. 1, Northern Liberties

events.name: Philadelphia Library Company: lecture by Prof. P. E. Chase
events.location: Lecture room of St. Thomas' Church, Fifth Street below Walnut, Philadelphia
events.description: Professor P. E. Chase, of this city, will lecture before the Philadelphia Library Company on Tuesday evening next, 6th inst., in the lecture room of St. Thomas' Church, Fifth Street below Walnut, commencing at 8 o'clock. Admission free. William P. Price, Secretary. (Chase is presumably Pliny E. Chase, a white Quaker scholar; not linked.)

events.name: United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. Joshua Woodlin Society: stated meeting
events.description: All the members of the United Beneficial Sisters of the Rev. Joshua Woodlin Society are requested to attend their stated meeting on Thursday evening next, January the 8th, 1863. By order of the President. Elizabeth Harris [VERIFY], President; Elizabeth Stokley [VERIFY: printed 'Stok?ly'], Secretary. (Officers named: new relative to the earlier standing notice.)

events.name: Elisha Weaver address at the A.M.E. Church, Burlington, N.J.
events.description: 'An Address of Great Importance': By divine permission, Rev. Elisha Weaver will deliver an address in the A. M. E. Church of Burlington, N. J., to the Mothers of all the colored churches in that city, and others; the young ladies and gentlemen, as well as the fathers, are invited, Tuesday night, January 6th, 1863. The Rev. Joseph Smith, the Elder in charge, and Brother Long [bare surname], who extended the invitation, have the tickets in hand.

events.name: Lecture by Prof. Reason for the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association
events.description: Prof. Reason (bare surname; of New York) lectured on Monday night [Dec. 29, 1862] in the Central Presbyterian Church for the benefit of the Social, Civil, and Statistical Association of Philadelphia; subject Civilization [VERIFY]. Praised as a scholar; manner mild and pleasant. Probably Charles L. Reason (identification not printed).

events.name: R. W. Grand Lodge of Pennsylvania (Prince Hall): fourth quarterly communication, election and installation
events.location: Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street below Pine, Philadelphia
events.description: Masonic Notice. The fourth quarterly communication was held at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh street below Pine, Dec. 1st, 1862, at which officers were elected and re-elected, and installed on St. John the Evangelist's Day, Dec. 27th, 1862, A. L. 5862. Brother J. Needham, R. W. G. Master; Jonathan Davis, M. D. [degree letters VERIFY], R. W. Deputy Grand Master; Nath'l L. Durham, R. W. Sen. G. Warden; Fred C. Revels [VERIFY], R. W. Jun. G. Warden; Theo Young, R. W. G. Treasurer; Aaron P. Faucett, R. W. G. Secretary. Appointments: Grand Chaplains, Rev. Brothers Frisby [bare surname], James Underdue [VERIFY], William G. Cooper. District Deputy Grand Masters: Francisco R. Belasques [VERIFY spelling], of Philadelphia, for Montgomery county; Thomas Early, of Harrisburg (Dauphin, Lycoming, Lancaster, Cumberland); Charles Cann [VERIFY], of Harrisburg (Franklin, Adams, Perry); John Griffiths, of Lewistown (Juniata, Mifflin, Centre, Blair, Huntingdon); George B. Vashon, of Pittsburg (Allegheny, Westmoreland, Fayette, Washington). Grand Lecturer, Francis R. Belasques [VERIFY]. Senior G. Deacon, Uriah Kelley [VERIFY]; Junior G. Deacon, Wm. Cooper; Grand Stewards, Joseph C. Grove [VERIFY] and William Williams; Grand Marshall, Jonathan C. Miller; Grand Sword Bearer, William Waters; Grand Pursuivant, Nathaniel Morgan; Grand Tyler, Lewis P. Rennis [VERIFY]. Committee on By-Laws: Jonathan Davis, Nathaniel Durham, F. R. Belasques, L. R. Seymour, J. T. Robinson. Committee on Land Marks: W. H. Riley, Wm. E. Gipson, Enos Shedd [VERIFY]. Committee on Correspondence: S. Morgan Smith, Redmond Faucett, Richard H. Gleaves, P. N. Judah, John G. Dutton. Committee on Finance: Wm. E. Gipson, Thomas Charnock, Ralph C. Gilmore [VERIFY middle initial], Charles Hettstock [VERIFY], Samuel C. Downing. Committee on Charity: John Coulter [VERIFY], George Woolford, Thos. C. Burton, Saml. L. Collins, Campbell Dickson [VERIFY]. Attest, Aaron P. Faucett, R. W. G. Secretary. Harrisburg, Lewistown and Pittsburg deputies are named in text only (non-Philadelphia).
attendees: R. W. Deputy Grand Master; Committee on By-Laws
R. W. Senior Grand Warden; Committee on By-Laws (as 'Nathaniel Durham')
Committee on Land Marks; Committee on Finance

events.name: R. W. Grand Lodge of New Jersey: annual communication and installation
events.description: Masonic Notice. Saturday, the 27th, being Saint Johns' day, the R. W. Grand Lodge of the State of New Jersey, at their annual communication held in the city of Burlington, installed: John F. King, R. W. G. M.; Albert C. Stevens, R. W. D. G. M.; James Bingess [VERIFY], G. S. W.; James Dolphin [VERIFY], G. J. W.; Ebenezer Men[?] [VERIFY], G. T.; Joshua Woodlin, G. Sec. Appointments: District Deputy G. M. John A. Lohes [VERIFY], for Salem; Henry H. Williams, for Camden and Gloucester; Joseph Jordan, for Cumberland; Charles Fauset [VERIFY], for Burlington and Mercer; Richard T. Levette [VERIFY], for Cape May; Peter D. Hodges for Middlesex and Essex; Charles Lopeman [VERIFY], S. D.; Caleb Jackson, J. D.; Henry Carter, S. Steward; Adam R. Dell, J. S.; Charles Williams, G. M.; Charles Gardner, G. T.; Isaac Wells, G. P.; Alfred H. Tucker, G. L. Committee on Land Marks: R. L. Davis [VERIFY], Freeman Gould, J. Woodlin. Committee on By-Laws: Joshua Woodlin, G. L. Davis, H. Williams. Attest, John F. King, R. W. G. M. Linked only: the Grand Master and Deputy, and Rev. Joshua Woodlin (Philadelphia Conference clergy).
attendees: R. W. Deputy Grand Master, N.J.
Grand Secretary, N.J.; Committee on By-Laws (also 'J. Woodlin', Committee on Land Marks)

events.name: Tillman Relief Association of Bordentown sends box to Union Relief Association of Bethel Church, Washington
events.description: The colored citizens of Bordentown organized the Tillman Relief Association for the contrabands in and around Washington, D. C. Officers: Rev. J. Young, President; Mr. J. Rnem [VERIFY, illegible], Treasurer; Mr. Y. Luen [VERIFY, illegible], Secretary. Committee: Mrs. E. Cullens [VERIFY], Mrs. A. Crippen, and Mrs. R. Wood. They filled a box with goods, clothing and groceries containing two hundred and forty pieces, and three dollars and forty cents' worth of groceries, sent on the 24th of December, 1862, to the Union Relief Association of Bethel Church, in the care of Rev. H. M. Turner, Washington, D. C., No. 93 South E Street.

events.name: Donation visit to the Christian Recorder
events.description: Card of thanks from Elisha Weaver and Mary C. Weaver to the committee of ladies who organized a donation visit to assist the Recorder and Book Concern; it did not realize as much as hoped. Messrs. Hall and Gordon (bare surnames) thanked for ham and turkey; Rev. Stephen Smith was the only preacher present, and dined. Date of the visit not stated (late Dec. 1862).

events.name: Emancipation Day (Jan. 1, 1863) services in Philadelphia's colored churches
events.location: Philadelphia: Bethel; First African Presbyterian (Mr. Gibb's Church, Seventh St.); St. Mary St. Church; Central Presbyterian (Rev. Mr. Reeve's Church, Lombard St.); St. Thomas'; the Baptist churches; Wesley Church, Lombard St.
events.description: 'Meetings and Demonstrations': In honor of the President's proclamation services were held, 'we believe,' in every colored church in Philadelphia. Bethel: meetings morning and night. The Presbyterian churches combined: at Mr. Gibb's Church in Seventh St. in the morning, at the St. Mary St. Church in the afternoon, and at eight in Rev. Mr. Reeve's Church, Lombard St. St. Thomas' held a meeting in the fore part of the day, and so did the Baptist churches. Wesley Church, Lombard St. (Rev. John A. Williams, pastor) had a strong demonstration morning, noon and night with 'some of the ablest speakers the city can afford': Rev. Walter [VERIFY] Jackson, friend Bond, Prof. [Green? illegible], Mr. Chester, of Harrisburgh, and others; 'here was witnessed the talent of the black man and the white.' The writer links Union successes (Murfreesboro) to the proclamation. Gibbs and Reeve given as surnames only (presumably Rev. Jonathan C. Gibbs and Rev. John B. Reeve; Mr. Chester of Harrisburg presumably T. Morris Chester): not linked. (Also named, reading uncertain: Walter Jackson [VERIFY] (speaker (Rev.)).)

events.name: Bethel Church: day of humiliation, fasting and prayer; watch-night meeting
events.description: The elders of Bethel, on the recommendation of the Committee of the Official Board, appointed Dec. 31, 1862 as a day of humiliation, fasting and prayer, that God would strengthen the President in his emancipation policy, give success to Federal arms, and change Northern prejudice. On the evening of the 31st (watch meeting) Bethel was crowded to overflowing, at least one-fourth of the congregation being whites. After a short sermon by Rev. Mr. Arkon [VERIFY, bare surname], Rev. Mr. Lockwood (white), missionary to the contrabands, held the audience spell-bound until a few minutes of twelve, when the whole congregation knelt in silent prayer to welcome in the new-born day of liberty. The choir sang 'Blow ye the trumpet, blow.' A collection was taken for the preacher, church and poor.

events.name: Bethel Church: New Year's Day thanksgiving for the Emancipation Proclamation
events.description: By previous arrangement New Year's Day was kept by the members of Bethel as a day of thanksgiving that God had directed the heart of Abraham Lincoln to grapple the institution of slavery. A committee of Wm. Scott, James Robinson, Alfred Lawrence, Morris Hall, Henry Gordon, James Gray [VERIFY], Abm. Fields arranged the programme and bought four large pound cakes, sliced on tables each side of the main aisle. Elder Campbell presided [bare surname; presumably Rev. J. P. Campbell, Bethel's pastor]. Thanksgiving sermons by Elder P. Gardner [VERIFY; probably Rev. Peter Gardiner] and Rev. H. Davis; the congregation partook of the cake and left 'a nice sum' for the poor, singing 'Blow ye the trumpet.' Evening services: 'a rich treat from Mr. Plumly, a tried friend of the oppressed' [bare surname; presumably B. Rush Plumly]. The day passed quietly. National flags hung from (colored) public houses: in Seventh Street below Lombard, Brown's Hotel, a very large flag and several small ones flung out by the Delmonico Association; another large one from the Hannibal House, Pine St., between 6th and 7th. 'The day was well observed, and will pass into history creditable to the colored people of Philadelphia.'

events.name: Jordantown (N.J.) quarterly meeting
events.description: Editor attended Jordantown Quarterly meeting on the last Sabbath of 1862 by invitation of Rev. Joseph H. Smith; brothers Smith and Joseph Long labor together on the circuit; Recorders sold and subscribers gained.

events.name: Burlington (N.J.) quarterly meeting
events.description: First Sabbath of the new year: brother Smith's quarterly meeting at Burlington, attended by Weaver, who preached morning and evening and was asked by Elder Smith to consecrate the Lord's supper; brother Long preached Saturday night (Jan. 3) and brother Smith Sabbath afternoon. Brother Smith's circuit gives the Recorder its largest circulation in the Philadelphia District.

events.name: Weaver's address to the mothers of Burlington
events.description: Follow-up to the Jan. 3 announcement: delivered Tuesday night, the 6th inst., in a hard storm, yet 'a goodly number' attended, far excelling 'our people here in the city of Philadelphia.'

events.name: Camden (N.J.) New Year's Eve and Contraband Relief Committee fair
events.description: Letter signed 'West Jersey': no public demonstration in Camden on New Year's Day; religious exercises on the eve as on former occasions, the clock in the Macedonia [A.M.E. church] watched with more than ordinary interest; an old fugitive (35 years free) said 'I have never felt free before to-day.' The Contraband Relief Committee held a fair during the holidays; proceeds not above fifteen dollars, articles furnished by stores on commission. No names given.

events.name: Trenton Circuit quarterly meetings
events.description: Rev. Wm. Moore's announcement (letter of Jan. 6, 1863): quarterly meetings Jan. 11th and 12th [VERIFY dates] at Pennington; Jan. 24th and 25th at Trenton; Jan. 31st and Feb. 1st at Lewisville. Free-will offering of $5 from the circuit ($1.50 from Pennington, of which 30 cents from the Pennington Sabbath School under Brother Light, superintendent, with five teachers; $3.50 from Mount Zion A.M.E. Church, Trenton). Brother James Saraby [VERIFY] acting as Recorder agent.

events.name: Book Concern Executive Committee meeting and hymn-book appeal
events.description: Editor and General Book Steward Elisha Weaver called the Executive Committee of the Book Concern together on Nov. 13, 1862. Finding only seven or eight hymn-books in store, the committee advised a new edition (about $500), asking each elder, deacon and preacher to take a free-will collection and forward it; 'We will answer for the Philadelphia district.' Signed William Moore, W. H. Waters [VERIFY], Stephen Smith, W. D. W. Schureman, Elisha Weaver, Ch'n. (A changed/new Book Concern notice relative to the Q4 1862 executive committee capture.)

events.name: Banneker Institute of Philadelphia: annual election
events.description: Annual election Jan. 14, 1863: President, Jacob C. White, Jr.; Vice President, Joel Selsey; Recording Secretary, St. Geo. R. Taylor; Corresponding Secretary, Octavius V. Catto; Treasurer, William H. Minton; Committee on Debates and Lectures, Joel Selsey (chairman), Parker T. Smith, J. Wesley Simpson. Attested by St. Geo. R. Taylor, Rec. Sec.
attendees: vice president; chairman, Committee on Debates and Lectures

events.name: Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania (Union Hall, 510 South Seventh): election and installation of officers
events.location: Their Hall (Union), No. 510 South Seventh Street, Philadelphia
events.description: 'Election of Officers', A. L. 5862, Philada., Dec. 27, A.D. 1862. At the Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania, held the 15th [VERIFY] instant for the election of officers, and installed on the 21st [VERIFY] instant at their Hall (Union), No. 510 South Seventh Street, these brethren were re-elected for one year: Joseph Wellington [VERIFY], M. W. G. Master; Emory Cromwell [VERIFY, printed 'Froubsan'?], R. W. D. G. Master; John Riton [VERIFY], R. W. S. G. Warden; Jonathan Miller, R. W. J. G. Warden; Isaiah Cropper, G. Treasurer; Daniel Johnson, G. Sec.; John Marothey [VERIFY], G. C. Sec.; Joseph Hart, S. G. Steward; Solomon Green [VERIFY], J. G. Steward; John Hutcheon [VERIFY], G. S. Bearer; Ishmael White, G. Marshall; David Hall, G. Pursuivant; Daniel Murray, G. Tyler; Rev. Bro. Henry Pugh, G. S. Chaplain; Rev. Bro. Wm. Parker, G. J. Chaplain; John Rhoads, G. M. Ceremonies; Wm. Winter, G. L. Master; Moses Wheeler, G. S. Deacon; Thomas Faucett, G. J. Deacon. Appointments: Committee on Land-Marks, John Rhoads, Moses Davis, Cyrus Black, Sr. [VERIFY]; By-Laws, Emanuel Cohen, Sr., Randall Pleasants, Sr. [VERIFY], Henry Thomas; Charity, Moses Young, Henry Harper, James Wilson; Finance, John Brown, Wm. D. Cooper, Samuel B. Saunders; Grievances, William Winters, David Waters, Dennis West, Jos. Hart, Thomas Vincent. Daniel Johnson, Secretary, No. 508 Hurst Street. This is a different body from the R. W. Grand Lodge of Pa. (Masonic Hall, S. Eleventh St.) reported Jan. 3; the very common names (James Wilson, John Brown, Henry Thomas) are listed here but not linked.
attendees: Senior Grand Steward; Committee on Grievances (as 'Jos. Hart')
Grand Master of Ceremonies; Committee on Land-Marks

events.name: St. Thomas' Church Sabbath School exhibition
events.description: 'Exhibition at St. Thomas' Church on last Monday night' (editorial report). The lecture room was crowded and many could not gain admittance; the writer was piloted by Mr. Price over the platform. The Sabbath School is under the Rev. William Alston, 'a countryman of ours, who is very much liked'; Mr. Revels [VERIFY] is the Superintendent of the Sabbath school. Singing and solos assisted by a melodeon, flute, bass violin and violin. A little miss, Louise Matthews [VERIFY], was 'the charm and attraction of all'; another little miss recited a piece about the little contrabands; Miss Cole [VERIFY] appeared on the stage and sang. Mrs. Wilkins [VERIFY] passed ice cream. It was half-past ten when the writer left.
attendees: Rev.; St. Thomas' Sabbath School is 'under' him (rector of St. Thomas')

events.name: Quarterly Meeting at Bethel Church
events.description: 'One of the most spirited Quarterly Meetings was held in Bethel on Sunday, the 25th.' A dense crowd at each service, with side benches and a standing audience. Our respected young brother, Redman Faucett, of the Union Church, preached in the morning at 10 o'clock (apparently his first sermon in Bethel; 'bids fair to be one of the most talented preachers in our Church'). Brother Maine of the Zion Mission preached in the afternoon ('came from the hot bed of slavery'). Brother Stanford, the Elder of Little Wesley, preached in the evening ('deserves the title of poet preacher').
attendees: preacher, of the Union Church (morning sermon)

events.name: Love feast at Bethel Church
events.description: 'Love Feast on Monday Evening. The church was densely crowded. Our friends from the Wharton street, St. John's, and the Central M. E. Church, were set down in front of the church by car loads.' The editor complains that the speaking was disorderly and blames 'ignorant class leaders'.

events.name: Lectures on the Seven Churches of Asia and their Epistles -- second lecture
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street, Philadelphia
events.description: 'The second lecture of the course will be delivered in the Wesley A. M. E. church, Hurst street, Philadelphia, on Sunday evening, the 1st of February, at half past 7 o'clock. Theme: The Divine Message to the Church of Ephesus.' Lecturer not named in the notice (presumably the Wesley pastor).

events.name: Preachers' Aid Society -- meeting called
events.description: 'Notice. All the members of the Preachers' Aid Society are hereby notified to meet on Wednesday, the 25th inst., in Bethel church, Philadelphia, at 9 o'clock, A. M., by order of the Vice President.' Signed Jeremiah G. Bulah [VERIFY].

events.name: Relief for the Contrabands -- Thomas Green's appeals at Union Bethel and Bethel
events.location: Union Bethel ('up town') and Bethel A.M.E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: 'Brother Thomas Green, of Washington, D. C., the President of the A. M. E. Union Association, is in our city. He set forth the claims of the Contrabands before the people last Wednesday night, in Union Bethel, up town, and Thursday night in Bethel church.' Readers are referred to the association's advertisement (its address appears on p2 col 7). A col 6 letter adds that Thomas E. Green, agent of the Union Relief Association of Union Bethel Church, Washington, left Washington last Friday, was in Baltimore, and was expected in Philadelphia 'about next Friday' and in New York the week after.

events.name: Sabbath of Feb. 8 in Philadelphia churches (Editorial Remarks)
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church and Wesley church, Lombard Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Editor's round of the churches 'last Sabbath': Bethel Church in the morning, a sensible discourse from a local brother of Zion Mission of the A. M. E. Church (congregation not as full as it should have been); in the afternoon Rev. Stephen Smith preached the funeral sermon of an old lady [name not given]; at night at Rev. Mr. Williams's (Wesley) church in Lombard Street, where Rev. Mr. Scott preached (his first time there since 1855) on Mark 14, followed by the Lord's Supper; the church was densely packed. 'This church, through the efforts of the pastor, Rev. John A. Williams, has advanced another step in improvement by introducing instrumental music into the church, a melodeon.'
attendees: pastor (Rev.), Wesley church, Lombard Street; introduced a melodeon

events.name: Banneker Institute lecture: Prof. A. M. Green, 'Lessons in the School of Mythology'
events.description: 'Philadelphia Items. A lecture was delivered before the Banneker Institute, at the St. Thomas' Lecture Room, on last Tuesday night, by Prof. A. M. Green. The subject was, Lessons in the School of Mythology.' The editor calls it a grand affair: 'As a political speaker, we must say, we have never heard his equal in Philadelphia.' At the close Mr. J. C. White, Jr., read a question for debate: 'Will the enlistment of colored men advance their political and social rights?' The disputants were Messrs. Sipsion [?], Weir, McCimb [?], and Bowers (surnames only as printed).
attendees: Banneker Institute; read the debate question (printed 'J. C. White, Jr.')

events.name: A Visit to Church: first colored (Wesley) M. E. Church, Lombard Street
events.location: First colored (Wesley) M.E. Church, Lombard Street, Philadelphia
events.description: Letter signed J. H., Philadelphia, Feb. 4th, 1863: 'I attended the first colored (Wesley) M. E. Church, Lombard street, on last Sabbath morning. Brother S. Primrose preached upon the occasion' (text James 4:7). 'In the afternoon the Rev. S. T. Jones preached a very good sermon. He first referred to the instrument installed into the choir' (vocal and instrumental music). 'Rev. Brother Gibson preached in the evening' (the writer was not there; a large audience).

events.name: Union Freedmen's Relief Association of West Philadelphia -- organizing meeting
events.location: Oak Street Baptist Church, West Philadelphia
events.description: A meeting of the colored people of West Philadelphia was held at the Oak street Baptist Church on Tuesday evening, February 24th, for the purpose of forming a Freedmen's relief association. The lecture room was packed. Professor A. M. Green addressed the people for more than an hour on his recent tour of thirteen weeks among the freedmen at Fortress Monroe, Alexandria and Washington. Resolved to organize permanently and to enroll the names of all present willing to labor. Rev. Charles M. Rodgers, pastor of the church, spoke, referring to his own family still in Virginia. Named 'Union Freedmen's Relief Association of West Philadelphia.' Officers: Rev. C. H. [sic; signature reads Charles M.] Rodgers, President; Robert Bentley, Esq., Vice President; David [surname illegible], Secretary; Elias Ferrell, Treasurer. A committee of three, Matthias Black, Charles Johnson and Emanuel Martine, appointed to draft a constitution. Signed Rev. Charles M. Rodgers, President; David [illegible], Esq., Secretary.
attendees: pastor, Oak Street Baptist Church; president (Rev.)

events.name: Hutchinson Family benefit concert for the Social, Civil and Statistical Association
events.description: Editorial notice (p2) and advertisement (p3): the Hutchinson Family ('Tribe of Asa') will sing for the benefit of the S. C. and Statistical Association of the colored people of Pennsylvania at Sansom Street Hall, Wednesday evening, March 11th; admission 25 cents; object, to aid the Contrabands. Ticket committee as printed: Isaiah C. Wears, W. Still, J. C. Gibbs, U. B. Vidal, Stephen Smith, J. C. White, Sr., Moses Wheeler, Franklin Turner, S. Morgan Smith, Henry Gordon, Robert Jones, W. P. Price, Morris Brown, C. H. Bustill, J. P. Clay, Parker T. Smith, Dr. J. H. Wilson.

events.name: Philadelphia Library Company lecture on nationality, and debate on colored men going to war
events.description: On last Tuesday night, Mr. Warner lectured before the Philadelphia Library Co., in St. Thomas' Church, on the subject of nationality: what constitutes a nation (men and women), the difference between Newfoundland and Ireland, the history of France, the two institutions of Freedom and Slavery, the Constitution and Jefferson's object. 'After he was through, the debate followed in relation to colored men going to the war.' Lecturer named only as 'Mr. Warner' (not linked).

events.name: Bible Association of Philadelphia among Colored People -- discourse at Bethel
events.description: The Bible Association of Philadelphia among Colored People is progressing finely. Rev. Mr. Asher, Baptist minister, is the President, and Rev. J. P. Campbell, Vice President. The President delivered a discourse in Bethel church on its objects, &c., last Thursday evening. (President named only as 'Rev. Mr. Asher', not linked.)

events.name: A. L. Stanford lecture at the Institute for Colored Youth
events.description: The Rev. A. L. Stanford lectured at the Institute for Colored Youth, on last Thursday night.

events.name: Literary Society of Bethel Church -- lecture by Dr. Wilson
events.description: Dr. Wilson of this city will lecture on next Thursday night, the 12th inst., before the Literary Society of Bethel Church. The lecture will be delivered in the above church. (Probably Dr. J. H. Wilson of the SCSA ticket committee in the same issue; not linked, bare surname.)

events.name: Bethel Sabbath School 26th anniversary exhibition
events.description: Exhibition. Bethel Sabbath School will celebrate their 26th anniversary at Sansom Street Hall, on next Thursday evening, the 19th instant ... There has been no pains nor labor spared on the part of the Christian Superintendent and gentleman, Mr. Seymour, in conjunction with the worthy managers, in the preparatory arrangements ... Mr. Seymour's name will be a sufficient guarantee. Admission (adults) twenty (20) cents; children, ten (10) cents. Tickets at the Bookstore (619 Pine street). Superintendent named only as 'Mr. Seymour' (not linked; possibly the M. L. B. Seymour who is secretary of the Daughters of Cornish, unconfirmed).

events.name: West Philadelphia (Schureman's circuit) protracted meeting
events.description: Under the charge of Rev. W. D. W. Schureman's circuit, [West Philadelphia] has been holding a protracted meeting. 'We have not yet learned what has been the result.' Also a protracted meeting at the Little Pine Street Baptist Church (Rev. Mr. Hamilton, pastor) reported Mar. 7 and Mar. 14.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference of the A. M. E. Church -- called
events.description: Notice to the Philadelphia and New England Conferences, signed W. Nazrey: The Philadelphia Annual Conference will meet the second Saturday in May, at 9 o'clock A. M., in Bethel Church, Sixth St., Phila. The New England Conference will meet the second Saturday in June, in Newport, R. I., in the A. M. E. Church, at 9 o'clock, A. M. Punctual attendance is requested. The members of each Conference District will pay strict regard to the financial collections per discipline. Invitation: Revs. Bishops Quinn and Payne are most cordially invited to meet with me at each. (Second Saturday in May 1863 = May 9, computed.) Separately (p1), a letter calls the General Conference committee on Bishop Payne's manuscript history of the A. M. E. Church (A. W. Wayman, Stephen Smith, J. P. Campbell, John M. Brown) to meet Wednesday, April 15th, at Bethel Church, Baltimore, and notes Philadelphia Conference members may attend.

events.name: Public meeting at Bethel Church on the present crisis; Frederick Douglass address; volunteers for the Massachusetts colored regiment
events.description: A public meeting was held on Wednesday evening, the 18th inst., in Bethel church, Sixth St., on the present crisis of this country, and the relation which colored persons should sustain to it. Officers appointed by resolution: President, Rev. J. P. Campbell. Vice Presidents, Rev. S. Smith, Rev. E. Weaver, Rev. W. D. W. Schureman, Messrs. M. Hall, F. Turner, U. B. Vidall [as printed], H. Shadd, B. Harris, D. B. Brown, and J. P. Burr [VERIFY]. Secretaries, Rev. E. D. Bassett, Rev. A. L. Stanford. Rev. W. D. W. Schureman addressed the throne of grace, after which the President introduced Mr. Frederick Douglass, who held the audience for at least an hour and a half on three questions: how the colored people should feel, think and act in regard to the present rebellion, setting forth the necessity of speedy action. The building, said to hold between two and three thousand persons, was comfortably filled; many white persons present. At the close Prof. Bassett offered a series of resolutions, passed without a dissenting voice. Messrs. Horace Potter, James Christopher, Edwin Johnson, Henry Johnson, and Francis Jones gave their names as volunteers for the Massachusetts regiment of colored soldiers. (Same column: Douglass also lectured the previous Tuesday night at the Institute for Colored Youth, crowded to capacity.)

events.name: Frederick Douglass lecture at the Institute for Colored Youth
events.description: Lectures by Frederick Douglass: the great hero and unfaltering Anglo-Saxon African opponent of American Slavery delivered a common sense lecture on last Tuesday night at the Institute for Colored Youth, which place was crowded to its utmost capacity. 'We hope that the pupils of the school, and all others who were present, have learned a lesson.' (Date computed: Tuesday before the Mar. 18 Bethel meeting.)

events.name: Funeral of Edward M. Thomas
events.description: Remains of Edward M. Thomas of Washington, D.C. (died New York Mar. 9, aged 42 or 43; president of the contemplated National Exhibition of the colored people, Oct. 1863) brought to Philadelphia to the house of Mr. Teagles [?], Tenth St., and deposited in the Olive Cemetery on Monday afternoon, Mar. 16, followed by a large procession in carriages and on foot of members of the church, the masonic fraternity and Good Samaritans. Thomas is a Washington man (text only, not linked).

events.name: Hutchinson Family concert for the First African Presbyterian Church
events.description: Benefit concert by the Hutchinson Family for the First African Presbyterian Church (Rev. Mr. Gibbs, pastor), Mar. 26, Sansom St. Hall; tickets 25 cts., children 15 cts., at the Book Store, Pine St.

events.name: Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School 26th anniversary
events.description: The great Anniversary came off at Sansom Street Hall, on the 19th inst. ... Every inch of the floor was occupied; at least one hundred had to go away. Exercises opened with prayer by Rev. Brother Jones, a Local Deacon of Zion Mission. Rev. Stephen Smith, the President of the Sabbath School Association, made some pertinent remarks. The school joined in a chorus. John W. Cromwell delivered the introductory address. The singing was conducted by Prof. P. Shadd; assisted at the piano by young Mr. Seymour. (Report of the event announced Mar. 14.)
attendees: president of the Sabbath School Association (Rev.)

events.name: Sabbath School Association of the Philadelphia District -- constitution committee called
events.description: A Call. At a convention of the Sabbath school Association of the Philadelphia District of the A. M. E. Church, which convened in Bethel Church, Sixth St., Phila., Nov. 12th, 1862, the following Committee were appointed on Constitution and By-laws: W. D. W. Schureman, J. P. Campbell, B. Brown, J. Woodlin, L. R. Seymour, Samuel J. Moore, A. L. Stanford, which committee are requested to meet in Bethel Church, on Wednesday, April 8th, 1863, at 10 o'clock, A. M., to draft a constitution and by-laws. W. D. W. Schureman, Ch'n.

events.name: Philadelphia Annual Conference -- Committee on Examination for elders' orders
events.description: All the travelling preachers who have not received Elders' Orders of the Philadelphia Annual Conference district are hereby requested to meet the following Committee on Examination, Bethel Church, May 8th, 1863 [printed 1859], at 10 o'clock, A. M.: W. D. W. Schureman, J. P. Campbell, A. L. Stanford, Com. Same page repeats Nazrey's call of the Conference (Bethel, second Saturday in May) and adds a Correction: in Bishop Nazrey's Salem circuit appointments it should read April, not May (so the Frankford funeral sermon for Rev. Richard Robinson falls on the first Sabbath in April [as corrected]).

events.name: Hutchinson Family concert in aid of the Union Baptist Church
events.description: The celebrated Hutchinson family will sing for the benefit of said Church on next Tuesday evening, March 31st, 1863 ... The pastor, Rev. James Hamilton, is a Christian and a gentleman ... Admittance 25 cents, children 10 cents. A refreshment table in the lecture-room. (Hamilton is the pastor called 'Rev. Mr. Hamilton' of the Little Pine Street Baptist church in Mar. 7 and 14.)
